text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.39% today after dropping sharply yesterday, but the stock remains down 8.84% over two weeks as refining margins have compressed. While crude oil prices ticked up on geopolitical tensions around Iran, the real pressure on the company comes from gasoline and diesel prices falling faster than oil costs, which squeezes the profit margin refiners earn on each barrel they process—and this squeeze is visible in the storage data, where gasoline and diesel inventories are building even as refineries run near full capacity at 92.8%.

The broader headwind is a global supply glut: the Trump administration's reported moves to allow more Russian diesel into the market and rising refining activity worldwide are adding fuel supply precisely when energy stocks are tumbling and consumers are heading into winter with prices finally starting to ease. For a refiner like Marathon, that's a double bind—high crude costs but limited pricing power on the products they sell.
